decisions.summary: land.claims_route sends a claims refusal claims_cure names (owed with no check in flight, or introduced) to the preflight's stops; any other to the deferred wait
decisions.why: Carries FR-001 and request item (1): the owed-with-none-in-flight refusal now stops before the gate. Routing 'introduced' claims to the preflight as well goes past the one case FR-001 names, but it adds an early stop and narrows nothing, so this mode gives it no ruling.

decisions.summary: Template evidence section ends 'THE VERDICT: [branch taken] - because [measurement]' plus the branch not taken; the trial form's doc says the review checks it
decisions.why: This is FR-002 and request item (2) as written. Naming the branch not taken adds to the line and takes nothing away.

decisions.summary: profile_stage writes meta.seat_search into .placed.json; perf_fanout.placed_of reads its integer counts alone
decisions.why: This is FR-003 and request item (3). The perf_fanout change follows from the new key, so that reader keeps working; it adds no scope.

decisions.summary: A leg carries (wall, cpu, {stage: seconds}); stage_rows prints every stage, largest move first, '*' past STAGE_SHARE = 1% of A's best roll
decisions.why: This is FR-004 and request item (4): every stage, for every form. Using A's roll pins down the spec's 'the roll's best time', and the sort order is presentation. FR-004 also asks that a leg with no stage times print its total alone; the plan does not drop that.

decisions.summary: make trial APPROVED= (TRIAL_APPROVED) fills the brief's approval line
decisions.why: This is FR-005 and request item (5a). The plan says nothing about FR-005's 'dated today', so that requirement stands and gets checked at implementation.

decisions.summary: stale_terms skips a candidate the diff rewrote only when the line it was rewritten from already named its subject (rewritten_from)
decisions.why: The request says 'the stale-terms check skipping lines the same diff rewrote', with no qualifier. Under the qualifier, a line the diff rewrote is still named when its earlier form did not mention the subject. That keeps existing behavior the GM did not ask to keep, and the bundle shows nothing in the GM's words that implies it. Nothing shows that skipping every rewritten line would be impossible or would defeat the request's purpose, which is to stop the check naming lines the author has already rewritten. Bundle defect: D5 cites 'FR-005-FR-007' as a range, and spec-cited.md holds FR-005 and FR-007 but not FR-006. spec-index.md's FR-006 and SC-005 lines are cut off before the words that would settle this. Cure: if the accepted FR-006 (or trial 439's report, which the GM approved as a list) states this qualifier, then D5b is already settled by the spec. In that case re-bundle with FR-006 in full, and D5b leaves the decisions list. Otherwise drop the qualifier, so that every line the same diff rewrote is skipped.

decisions.summary: ratchet.slowdown (loop on XDIST_WORKERS processes, best of 3 rounds' slowest over the pinned 0.12 s, at least 1) is measured only for a run at or over the ceiling, and divides quick's run before the verdict
decisions.why: FR-007 says the loop runs at the check. The plan runs it only when the raw run is at or over 15 s. The slowdown is never below 1, so dividing a run already under the ceiling cannot change the ceiling verdict, and the GM's words are about the ceiling failing under load. For every run the ceiling judges, the outcome is identical, so the gate is implied by the request. Two conditions go on record. (1) FR-007 asks the output to print the raw time, the slowdown and the normalized time. Under the gate, a run under the ceiling has no measured slowdown, so the output must say so (for example 'slowdown not measured: under the ceiling'); dropping it silently is not allowed. (2) This ruling assumes the ceiling is the only comparison in feature 171 that load can trip. If 171 also fails a raw run against the baseline below 15 s, the gate leaves that comparison raw, and the ruling does not hold. The bundle cannot settle (2).

decisions.summary: Performance bookends: none, because no engine code a roll runs changes
decisions.why: All the changes are tooling; nothing the GM asked for touches a roll.

decisions.summary: Constitution Check: VI by the named tests and real runs; X by the coverage floor on the changed l7r/ tools; feature 171's ceiling and baseline unchanged
decisions.why: Restates FR-007's 'ceiling and baseline unchanged' and settles nothing new.

decisions.summary: One task in five parts and one landing; done means the named tests, a real quick A/B with stage rows, and research/quick-calibration.md
decisions.why: Covers all five items the GM asked for, and the measurement FR-007 asks for.

decisions.summary: land.claims_route sends a claims refusal claims_cure names (owed with no check in flight per claims_flight.live, or introduced) to the preflight's stops; any other refusal to the deferred wait.
decisions.why: Request item (1) and FR-001: the owed-with-none-in-flight refusal moves before the gate. An introduced claim has no check in flight either, so routing it too is the same refusal, and FR-001 says the cheap refusals 'include' it. A claim with a check in flight still waits, which the request does not ask to change.

decisions.summary: The trial template's evidence section ends 'THE VERDICT: [branch taken] - because [measurement that took it]' plus the branch not taken; the trial form's doc says the review checks it.
decisions.why: Request item (2) and FR-002 almost word for word. Naming the branch not taken is what lets the review check the verdict against the rule's branches, as FR-002 asks.

decisions.summary: profile_stage writes meta.seat_search into .placed.json; perf_fanout.placed_of reads only its integer counts.
decisions.why: Request item (3) and FR-003. The perf_fanout change only keeps the one existing reader of the sidecar working with the new key. It adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Each leg carries (wall, cpu, {stage: seconds}), from the worker's roll in the quick and subset forms and from the snapshot legs in the full form; stage_rows prints every stage, largest move first, with * past STAGE_SHARE (1% of A's best roll).
decisions.why: Request item (4) and FR-004: every form, every stage, the 1% marker. 'A's best roll' is a reading of FR-004's 'the roll's best time' and does not narrow it. The ordering is presentation. The total-only fallback for a leg with no stage times stays in FR-004, and D4 does not contradict it.

decisions.summary: make trial APPROVED= (TRIAL_APPROVED) fills the brief's approval line, dated today.
decisions.why: Request item (5), 'make trial APPROVED=', and FR-005 as written.

decisions.summary: stale_terms skips a candidate the diff rewrote from a line already naming its subject (rewritten_from); a line the diff inserted, or rewrote to bring the subject in, is still searched, quoting FR-006's own condition.
decisions.why: Request item (5), 'the stale-terms check skipping lines the same diff rewrote', and FR-006. The previous round's finding is cured: D5 now cites FR-006 by itself and quotes its condition in full, including the clause that inserted lines and lines rewritten to bring the subject in are still searched. Nothing outside that condition is spared.

decisions.summary: ratchet.slowdown (the loop on XDIST_WORKERS forked processes, best of 5 rounds' slowest, over the pinned 0.12 s, floor 1) runs only for a quick run at or over the 15 s ceiling and divides that run before the verdict, which prints raw, slowdown and net. A run under the ceiling is judged raw and prints that its slowdown was not measured.
decisions.why: This narrows FR-007's output clause: a run under the ceiling does not print a measured slowdown or a normalized time. The GM's words are 'quick's 15 s ceiling failing under load', and their purpose is to stop the ceiling failing a run because of load. FR-007's own floor ('never below 1') means the normalized time is never above the raw time, so a run under the ceiling passes on either comparison and no verdict can change. The purpose is therefore untouched. The output says what was compared ('slowdown not measured'), so it does not mislead. Best of 5 rounds matches how the pin was taken (its one-shot label: 6 processes, best of 5 rounds, load 1.0), so the quotient compares like with like; this is method and stays within FR-007.

decisions.summary: Feature 171's other check on quick, the 60 s QUICK_BUDGET, stays raw.
decisions.why: The request names only 'quick's 15 s ceiling', and FR-007 changes 'the quick gate's time check' with the ceiling and baseline otherwise unchanged. Leaving the budget alone keeps to the request. Normalizing it too would be unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: Preamble, Summary, Technical Context, Performance bookends (none: tools only), Constitution Check, T01 approach (one task, five parts, the step-by-step measurement table, the calibration figures), Project Structure, Complexity Tracking.
decisions.why: These restate the five items and their FRs. They decide nothing the spec leaves open beyond order and file placement. The figures carry one-shot labels (0.12 s; 2.13x and 2.24x, measured 2026-10-27, with their methods) or a CONVENTION (15 s from the GM's words, 1%, 60 s, 100%).

decisions.summary: One task in five parts: the GM's five improvements in one task
decisions.why: The request asks for all five tooling improvements; one task with one part per improvement keeps all five and adds no extra work. How the work is ordered is not a scope decision.

decisions.summary: Green: landed with its tests and real runs. Red: record what failed, set the task down, and rule any 'cannot be done' claim through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: The red exit drops nothing on its own authority. A claim that an item cannot be done goes to the arbiter instead of being carved out by the session, which is the opposite of a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Budget: one landing
decisions.why: How the work is landed; it adds nothing to the request and takes nothing away.

decisions.summary: Done when the listed tests pass, a quick A/B prints its stage rows, and research/quick-calibration.md records that the slowdown tracks load (suite 2.13x, loop 2.24x, one-shot label 2026-10-27 with method)
decisions.why: Each condition is an SC or FR-007's own one-shot measurement. The figures carry a dated one-shot label with its method (quiet and with 16 busy processes). A real A/B run checks FR-004 on a live roll; it is verification of the requested item, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Each step measured by its own test file (claims stop, verdict line/APPROVED=, seat counters, every stage, stale terms, quick net of load)
